com.julien-dubois.bootui:bootui-quarkus-hibernate-integration-tests 1.12.0 发布, Minimal, Docker-free Quarkus app that adds quarkus-hibernate-orm (on an in-memory H2 database) on
        top of the bootui-quarkus extension and proves the Hibernate (ORM mapping) advisor light-up end to end:
        the app's mapped @Entity classes are read from the EntityManagerFactory metamodel by the engine
        JpaMetamodelReader (via the capability-gated QuarkusEntityDiscovery), the shared engine HibernateScanner
        runs its curated rule registry on POST /bootui/api/hibernate/scan, and the QuarkusHibernatePropertyLookup
        maps the engine's config keys onto the quarkus.hibernate-orm.* namespace (proving, in particular, that the
        Spring-only Open-Session-in-View rule HIB-CONFIG-001 stays inert). Kept separate from
        bootui-quarkus-integration-tests (which deliberately has NO Hibernate ORM) so the ORM-absent
        not-configured path and the ORM-present scan path are each proven in isolation — the same split used for
        the SmallRye-Health and OpenTelemetry present/absent coverage.

com.julien-dubois.bootui:bootui-quarkus-flyway-integration-tests 1.12.0 发布, Minimal, Docker-free Quarkus app that adds quarkus-flyway + quarkus-jdbc-h2 (in-memory) on top
        of the bootui-quarkus extension and proves the Flyway panel light-up: the migration history read from
        the application's active io.quarkus.flyway.runtime.FlywayContainer beans by the QuarkusFlywayProvider is
        shaped by the shared engine FlywayService, and the panel is surfaced on
        GET /bootui/api/flyway/migrations. Kept separate from bootui-quarkus-integration-tests (which
        deliberately has NO quarkus-flyway, so the capability gate keeps the flyway panel unavailable) so the
        flyway-present and flyway-absent paths are each proven in isolation — the same split used for the
        Cache-present/absent and SmallRye-Health-present/absent coverage.

com.julien-dubois.bootui:bootui-quarkus-email-integration-tests 1.12.0 发布, Minimal, Docker-free Quarkus app that adds quarkus-mailer on top of the bootui-quarkus
        extension and proves the Email Viewer panel light-up: an outgoing message sent through the
        application's Mailer fires a io.quarkus.mailer.SentMail CDI event that the QuarkusEmailCapture observer
        maps into the shared engine EmailCaptureService, so the panel is surfaced on GET /bootui/api/email with
        working detail + .eml download reads and a DELETE clear action. Kept separate from
        bootui-quarkus-integration-tests (which deliberately has NO quarkus-mailer, so the class-presence gate
        keeps the email panel unavailable) so the mailer-present and mailer-absent paths are each proven in
        isolation — the same split used for the cache-present/absent coverage. The default test-mode mailer is
        mock (quarkus.mailer.mock defaults to true under LaunchMode.TEST), so no SMTP server or Docker is
        needed; the SentMail event still fires in mock mode.

com.julien-dubois.bootui:bootui-quarkus-cache-integration-tests 1.12.0 发布, Minimal, Docker-free Quarkus app that adds quarkus-cache (Caffeine) on top of the
        bootui-quarkus extension and proves the Cache panel light-up: the live cache topology read from the
        application's io.quarkus.cache.CacheManager by the QuarkusCacheProvider is shaped by the shared engine

        bootui-quarkus-integration-tests (which deliberately has NO quarkus-cache, so the capability gate keeps
        the cache panel unavailable) so the cache-present and cache-absent paths are each proven in
        isolation — the same split used for the SmallRye-Health-present/absent and Micrometer-present/absent
        coverage.

        on top of the bootui-quarkus extension and proves the Liquibase panel light-up: the change-log history

        gate keeps the liquibase panel unavailable) so the liquibase-present and liquibase-absent paths are each
        proven in isolation — the same split used for the Cache-present/absent and SmallRye-Health-present/absent
        coverage.

com.julien-dubois.bootui:bootui-quarkus-prod-shell-guard-integration-tests 1.12.0 发布, Holds the one test in the whole bootui-quarkus-integration-tests reactor that boots a genuine
        LaunchMode.NORMAL (production) artifact via QuarkusProdModeTest, proving BootUiProdShellGuardFilter
        actually 404s /bootui and /bootui/** in a real production process (not just LaunchMode.TEST, which is
        all every @QuarkusTest elsewhere in this reactor can exercise). Kept in its own module/JVM fork on
        purpose: Quarkus's own test-framework ExclusivityChecker throws IllegalStateException if a
        QuarkusProdModeTest and a @QuarkusTest run in the same JUnit Platform launcher session (i.e. the same
        Surefire fork), so this test cannot live alongside base's (or any other submodule's) @QuarkusTest
        classes. Never published.

com.julien-dubois.bootui:bootui-quarkus-health-integration-tests 1.12.0 发布, Minimal, Docker-free Quarkus app that adds quarkus-smallrye-health on top of the bootui-quarkus
        extension and proves the Health panel light-up: a custom MicroProfile @Liveness HealthCheck is read in
        process via SmallRyeHealthReporter, mapped by QuarkusHealthProvider onto the neutral HealthNodeDto, and
        surfaced on GET /bootui/api/health by the shared engine HealthService. Kept separate from
        bootui-quarkus-integration-tests (which deliberately has NO SmallRye Health) so the SmallRye-absent
        setup-guidance path and the SmallRye-present capture path are each proven in isolation — the same split
        used for the OpenTelemetry-present/absent telemetry coverage.

        extension set on its classpath to prove BootUI panel light-up in isolation: the base module deliberately
        has no optional extensions (everything fails closed), and each per-extension module adds exactly one
        (otel, health, micrometer, scheduler, cache, flyway, liquibase, datasource). The Hibernate module also

        refuses to mix that mechanism with @QuarkusTest in the same Surefire fork.

com.julien-dubois.bootui:bootui-quarkus-security-integration-tests 1.12.0 发布, Minimal, Docker-free Quarkus app that adds the quarkus-security extension on top of the
        bootui-quarkus extension and proves the Security Logs panel light-up: with quarkus.security.events.enabled
        the CDI security events fired on authentication/authorization are captured by QuarkusSecurityEventCapture
        into the shared SecurityEventBuffer, assembled by the neutral SecurityLogsService and surfaced on
        GET /bootui/api/security-logs, with the panel reported available in the manifest. Kept separate from
        bootui-quarkus-integration-tests (which has NO security extension) so the security-absent unavailable path
        and the security-present capture path are each proven in isolation. Also adds quarkus-opentelemetry (like
        the sibling otel module) so a real server-span trace id is available at capture time, proving the Live
        Activity feed's security correlation: a captured security event nests under the REQUEST entry sharing its
        trace id and stamps that request's securedPrincipal.

com.julien-dubois.bootui:bootui-quarkus-datasource-integration-tests 1.12.0 发布, Minimal, Docker-free Quarkus app that adds a JDBC datasource (quarkus-jdbc-h2, backed by
        Agroal) on top of the bootui-quarkus extension and proves the Database Connection Pools panel light-up:
        the live Agroal pool configuration and AgroalDataSourceMetrics read by the QuarkusAgroalConnectionPoolProvider
        are mapped into the shared HikariPool* wire contract by the engine ConnectionPoolService, the JDBC URL /
        username are masked through the shared SecretMasker, and the panel is surfaced on
        GET /bootui/api/database-connection-pools/pools (plus the per-pool /snapshot route). Kept separate from
        bootui-quarkus-integration-tests (which deliberately has NO datasource, so the AGROAL capability gate
        keeps the panel unavailable) so the datasource-present and datasource-absent paths are each proven in
        isolation — the same split used for the cache-present/absent and SmallRye-Health-present/absent coverage.
